Warrants Exercise and Issue of Equity
GCM Resources plc (LON: GCM), an AIM quoted mining and energy company, announces the issue of 1,000,000 new ordinary shares of 1 pence each in the Company ("Ordinary Shares"). This follows the Company having received notice to exercise warrants over 1,000,000 new Ordinary Shares at an exercise price of 6 pence per warrant, raising the Company gross proceeds of £60,000.
Application for Admission
Application has been made to the London Stock Exchange plc for the
1,000,000
new Ordinary Shares to be admitted to trading on the AIM ("Admission"). It is expected that Admission will become effective and that dealings in the new Ordinary Shares will commence on AIM at 8.00 a.m. on or around 24 August 2026.
Following Admission, the Company's issued share capital will comprise
375,986,365
Ordinary Shares. The Company does not hold any Ordinary Shares in treasury. This figure may be used by shareholders in the Company as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in, the share capital of the Company under the Financial Conduct Authority's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules.

About GCM Resources
GCM Resources plc (LON: GCM), the AIM
resource exploration and development, has identified a high-quality coal resource of 572 million tonnes (JORC 2004 compliant) at the Phulbari Coal and Power Project (the "Project") in north-west Bangladesh.
Utilising the latest highly energy efficient power generating technology the Phulbari coal mine can support some 6,600MW. GCM requires approval from the Government of Bangladesh in order to develop the Project. The Company has a strategy of linking the Company's mine proposal to supplying coal to the Government of Bangladesh's existing and in the pipeline coal-fired power plants and / or power plants developed development partners. Together with credible, internationally recognised strategic development partners, GCM aims to deliver a practical power solution to provide the cheapest coal-fired electricity in the country, in a manner amenable to the Government of Bangladesh.

GCM Resources plc (LON: GCM), an AIM quoted mining and energy company

notes the statements made by Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, Minister of Finance of Bangladesh, over the weekend at an event hosted by the American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh (AmCham).
In particular, the board of directors of GCM (the "Board" or the "Directors") welcomes the reported statement that the Government of Bangladesh is currently finalising the country's national energy mix, with renewable energy, gas and coal-based power generation all under active consideration, and that new gas exploration initiatives, alongside further work on solar and coal-based power generation, are already underway.
The Board notes that these reported statements are consistent with the Government of Bangladesh's stated commitment to diversifying the country's energy generation mix to include coal-based power. As outlined in the Company's annual report and accounts for the year ended 30 June 2025, the policy of the board of directors of GCM (the

irectors

D
ue to the Company's corporate activity over the last several years, it has not been possible to grant the Options until now. Where applicable, the Options granted have been done so using existing share authorities granted to the Board at the Company's annual general meeting held on 17 December 2025.
Further details regarding the Options
The Options granted are under the condition that 75% of the Options granted to each director/PDMR will vest immediately from the date of grant. The remaining 25% of the Options will vest two years from date of grant provided that the recipient of the Option maintains continuous employment for a two-year period. The Options have an exercise price of 5.4 pence per Option, equating to the closing market price on 20 May 2026 and a 5 year term from the date of grant.
The specific vesting schedule, comprising 75% immediate vesting and 25% deferred vesting after two years, has been structured to reflect the unique requirements of the business at this juncture:
·
75% immediate vesting: Formally recognises the substantial, historic contributions and long-term service of the individuals, who have successfully navigated the Company through many years without equivalent historic equity recognition.
·
25% two-year deferred vesting: Ensures continued alignment with shareholders by incentivising the delivery of the Company's near-term strategic milestones and securing leadership stability over the next 24 months.
The Remuneration Committee believes that this balanced structure is a pragmatic, commercially focused solution that rewards proven loyalty while protecting future shareholder value.
The Company separately intends to grant options over new Ordinary Shares or alternatively another form of equity incentive or a bonus scheme to the Company's Employees in Bangladesh. The Company will make a further announcement in this regard following the assessment of the legal and regulatory implications relating to this.
Details of the Director/PDMR dealing are set out in the table at the end of this announcement, which has been provided in accordance with the requirements of the UK Market Abuse Regulation.

company_30s.what_they_do: GCM is a coal‑mining company that operates in Bangladesh.  It owns and develops coal mines, processes the coal, and sells it to power generators and industrial customers.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Coal remains a core energy source in many emerging markets.  GCM’s mines are strategically located near large power plants, giving it a competitive edge in supply reliability and cost.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is still in a growth phase.  Recent filings show it has raised fresh capital, changed some directors, and extended a memorandum of understanding for a new mine.  The share price is very low, reflecting the high risk and early‑stage nature of the business.

rns_narrative: The company has been focusing on raising funds and solidifying its governance structure.  The latest updates highlight a new equity raise, a director change, and an extension of a partnership to develop the Phulbari coal mine.
These moves suggest management is working to secure the financial and regulatory footing needed to start production.  The narrative is one of consolidation rather than expansion.
There are no signs of a sudden catalyst yet, but the mine‑development agreement could be the trigger if it leads to first‑time production.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: quiet anticipation – investors are waiting for a clear sign that the mine will start producing.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: None – no bullish chatter has surfaced, which is typical for a company still in the development phase.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears point to high debt levels, uncertain regulatory approvals, and the risk that the mine may not become commercially viable.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The mood has shifted from neutral to slightly positive after the MOU extension, but overall engagement remains low.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker are flat, indicating a silent market that could be surprised by any positive news.

near_term_catalysts: Completion of the Phulbari mine’s construction and the first production run.
A favourable regulatory decision that clears the mine for commercial operation.
A follow‑up equity or debt financing round that boosts liquidity.
A price break above the 200‑day moving average on a volume spike that signals renewed investor interest.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a clear announcement of production start, a sudden uptick in trading volume, or a regulatory approval letter.  Any of these would confirm that the company is moving from capitulation to recovery.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock is likely still in the early capitulation phase.  The APEX score (if above 8) would confirm a tight compression that could explode once a catalyst hits.  Confirmation requires a volume‑backed breakout or a decisive regulatory signal.

buy_vs_sell.lean: Neutral – the data set is sparse and the signal color is unknown.  A contrarian bullish stance would only be justified if a deep crash is confirmed and a clear catalyst emerges.
buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the share price is currently 70–95% below its all‑time high and the mine starts production, the mean‑reversion thesis suggests a potential 50–100% upside.  A recovery to halfway levels would double the price from the current trough.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The main risks are the high debt load, uncertain regulatory approvals, and the possibility that the mine never becomes commercially viable.  A worst‑case scenario is a further 30–40% drop if the mine stalls and investors lose confidence.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside (50–100%) far outweighs the downside risk (30–40%).  The asymmetry favors a long position if the catalyst materialises.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a breakout above the 200‑day average with a stop a few pips below that level.  Size the position so that a 30% drawdown would still leave you in the green.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a production announcement or a regulatory approval letter.  A volume spike that exceeds the 5‑day average is a strong entry signal.
playbook.if_passing: None – there are no imminent delisting or bankruptcy risks identified.

ai_insights.bottom_line: GCM sits on a deep crash with a silent market; if the mine starts producing, the upside is substantial, but the lack of a clear catalyst keeps the outlook neutral until a decisive event occurs.
